articles.title: Astros’ System Wins Two Titles in 2026
articles.summary: Astros system wins two championships for first time in more than a decade.
articles.body:
The Astros minor league system has had its ups and downs over the last few years. After a great stretch that helped fuel the dynasty in Houston from 2017 through 2023, the farm system took a hit from graduations, trades and players moving up to the big leagues.

The 2026 season might be the start of the turnaround.

In 2026, Astros minor league affiliates took home two championships, marking the first time two teams in the system won league titles in the same season since 2015, when Triple-A Fresno and Rookie-level Greeneville both won championships.

While winning minor league championships doesn't necessarily mean the big league club will have success, building a winning culture is important, and the Astros did just that this year at the lower levels of the system.

The Florida Complex League Astros, Houston's Rookie-level affiliate, put together a historic season in 2026. The club went 42-11 during the regular season, setting a new franchise record, before running through the postseason and winning all three games on its way to the FCL championship.

The Fayetteville Woodpeckers, Houston's Single-A affiliate, had an impressive turnaround of their own. Fayetteville struggled out of the gate, starting the season 3-12 and enduring a rough first half. But things changed quickly in the second half.

The Woodpeckers caught fire, winning 13 games in a row at one point and finishing the second half with a 39-25 record. Like the FCL Astros, Fayetteville dominated in the postseason, sweeping both series behind elite starting pitching and timely hitting to capture the Carolina League championship.

The 2026 draft class also provided Fayetteville with a huge boost down the stretch, giving the Woodpeckers an influx of talent unlike anything they had seen earlier in the season.

The ultimate goal is for these prospects to develop into players who can help the Astros compete for World Series titles. But creating a winning culture and playing meaningful games in the minor leagues matters, too.

With two championships in 2026 and more talent beginning to emerge throughout the system, there are signs that the Astros farm system is headed in the right direction.

articles.title: Nor'easter concerns lead NYRA to cancel weekend racing at Belmont Park
articles.summary: Concerns over the nor'easter expected to impact Long Island this weekend have led NYRA to cancel the Saturday and Sunday racing cards at Belmont Park.
articles.body:
Racing at Belmont Park on Saturday and Sunday has been canceled due to the forecast of a powerful nor'easter expected to bring heavy rain and wind to Long Island throughout the weekend, the New York Racing Association announced Friday.

The move was made with the National Weather Service placing Long Island under a wind advisory for both Saturday and Sunday. Current forecasts call for sustained high winds with gusts exceeding 50 mph.

NYRA also announced Friday that it received approval from the state Gaming Commission to conduct live racing on the next two Wednesdays, Sept. 30 and Oct. 7. The association previously announced it received approval to conduct racing on Oct. 14, 21 and 28 as make-up dates for card cancellations from earlier in the year.

The addition of the make-up dates means that Belmont Park, which officially reopened Sept. 18 following a three-year, $555 million renovation , will operate on a Wednesday through Sunday racing calendar throughout October.

The most recent NYRA card to be canceled was July 29 at Saratoga Race Course , when that Wednesday program was called off due to torrential rainfall impacting Saratoga Springs and the rest of the Capital Region.

Tickets and pre-paid parking for Saturday and Sunday purchased directly through NYRA sales, Ticketmaster or FEVO are eligible for a refund or ticket credit, while tickets purchased through third-party vendors are not eligible for refunds from NYRA.

There were six stakes races scheduled for Saturday and Sunday at Belmont, all of which will be brought back for this coming Thursday's card. Those races are the Grade 1, $500,000 Joe Hirsch Turf Classic; the Grade 2, $500,000 Flower Bowl; the Grade 3, $250,000 Vosburgh; the Grade 2, $250,000 Gallant Bloom; the Grade 3, $200,000 Belmont Turf Sprint; and the Grade 3, $200,000 Winter Memories.

The added card for this coming Wednesday will offer overnight races that were originally scheduled for the Saturday and Sunday cards.

articles.title: Brock Bowers Misses Practice, Causing Fantasy Football Chaos And Uncertainty Surrounding Michael Mayer
articles.summary: The latest injury update on Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers and the fantasy impact.
articles.body:
In what has surprised many, but shouldn't have surprised anyone, Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers was not spotted at practice today. After a promising week and reassurance from Raiders head coach Klint Kubiac, Bowers is now in danger of missing another game in Week 3.

If you have been following us, you know that we have expected Bowers to come back in Week 4 at the earliest all along. Nevertheless, this does not necessarily mean Bowers will not play this week, but it certainly isn't a positive sign.

The worst-case scenario would be if he's a game-time decision with the team playing in the late-afternoon games on Sunday. We would not advise relying on Bowers this week. If you do not have a reliable pivot option that you can swap in for him, then just go with another option.

Even if Bowers does start this week, we aren't confident that he'll play well. We saw him struggle last season after dealing with a knee injury. There is a real chance that even if he is active, Bowers will have his snap count limited.

Under know circumstance, should you be expecting to plug an elite TE1 into your lineup this week. Not only are their opponents, the New Orleans Saints, a tough matchup, allowing the 10th-fewest fantasy points to tight ends this season, but we have almost no confidence that Bowers is healthy enough to be a productive fantasy tight end.

Mayer is the ideal pivot option for the Raiders this week. If Bowers is out and Mayer plays, Mayer should be a good enough option. Otherwise, you'll likely be stuck deciding who to stream between options like Cade Otton and Evan Engram.

The real issue will be if Bowers plays and you own both Bowers and Mayer. Then you are in a real pickle.

We would not want to start Mayer if Bowers is active, but they will likely just split the work and cannibalize each other. Hopefully, the Raiders announce early that they are giving Bowers another week or two to get fully healthy, and you can plug Mayer into your lineup with confidence.

articles.title: Ryan Fox sings karaoke on Internationals team bus while Tom Kim tries to nap

MEDINAH, IL – Presidents Cup International Team Captain Geoff Ogilvy said on Wednesday that what happens in the team room, stays in the team room. But what happens on the team bus appears to be fair game and going viral in the golf social media community.

Will Wilcox, the caddie for International Team member Sungjae Im, posted a video of British Open champion Ryan Fox singing karaoke on the team's long bus ride as fellow team member Tom Kim catches a nap.

Fox, a New Zealand native, is singing the Kenny Rogers hit "The Gambler." Kudos to Skratch Golf's Claire Rogers on bringing the video to the masses.

Fox, a 39-year-old Presidents Cup rookie, lost his debut match with Adam Scott on Thursday in a four-ball match. He's scheduled to play in the third match of Friday's foursomes with Min Woo Lee against Collin Morikawa and Wyndham Clark of the U.S.

Kim is partnering with Si Woo Kim for the second straight and will face Patrick Cantlay and Xander Schauffele.

articles.title: Steven Wright: Athlete of the Week: Shandon Garrett, Eaton
articles.summary: One of Shandon Garrett’s favorite parts of playing volleyball is the back-and-forth nature of matches. Being in control of setting up points with her teammat...
articles.body:
One of Shandon Garrett's favorite parts of playing volleyball is the back-and-forth nature of matches. Being in control of setting up points with her teammates keeps the game moving — until it comes to a screeching halt when she finishes a spike to the opponent's side of the court.

Garrett is a senior volleyball player at Eaton. In a three-match stretch against Greenville, Brookville and Dayton Christian, she averaged 21.3 kills and 14.6 digs per match and had a 48.8 percent attack percentage in 10 total sets.

For her efforts, Garrett was named the Dayton Daily News Athlete of the Week, presented by Orthopaedic Institute of Dayton, for Sept. 14-20, earning the honor through reader voting at DaytonDailyNews.com .

"I was actually in the doctor when I found out that I was nominated for it, and I showed my dad and I was like, 'Did you see this?' I was just so excited," Garrett said.

Garrett's efforts were needed to help the Eagles pull out victories in those matches. No set was determined by more than seven points over the three matches and meant every point counted. Her numbers improved as the week went on, starting with 18 kills against Greenville and going up to 26 in the win over Dayton Christian.

She kept it going into the Monday, Sept. 21 match against Kenton Ridge with a 26-kill, 25-dig double-double.

"I feel like I play with confidence and I have confidence in myself on the court," she said. "And I'm quite loud. I feel like I'll stick up for my team if something goes down where I'm gonna stick up for ya'll. I love it."

Being more vocal has come with gaining a team-oriented mindset as she progresses through her senior year with seven teammates she's been with for the past six years.

She's also committed herself to finding ways to help others in practice as part of that process.

Garrett is committed to play volleyball at Cleveland State. She has finished in the top-five of the Southwestern Buckeye League in kills after each of her three seasons and is challenging for the top spot this year. She has amassed more than 1,300 kills in her four-year career, breaking the school record for the category along the way.

"I played middle pretty much all the season last year and I really liked it. … There's more going back and forth and it's a lot more running in the middle, but I do kind of like being stationary and on the outside," Garrett said.

Being close to Lake Erie was a positive for choosing CSU and she joked it would be neat if a match was scheduled to play on the lake during her upcoming time with the Vikings.

Until then, she wants to enjoy making more fun memories with her current friends — and throw down more spikes on opponents along the way.
